stated: Reform UK will deport offenders holding dual citizenship, make child grooming an aggravating offence, improve safeguarding of victims, and deny bail for grooming gang offenders.

source.quote: Stop Child Grooming Gangs Deport offenders holding dual citizenship. Make child grooming an aggravating offence. Improve safeguarding of victims and vulnerable. No bail for grooming gang offenders.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets a category of serious sexual crime against children via sentencing (aggravating offence), pre-trial detention (bail denial), deportation of convicted dual nationals, and improved victim safeguarding — squarely within crime, justice, and victim support.

Mandatory bail denial (limiting individual due-process assessment) and deportation reserved for dual nationals (creating a two-tier criminal penalty based on citizenship status) raise non-negligible equal-treatment and due-process concerns warranting a real verdict.

Automatic denial of bail for a defined category of offenders expands state pre-trial detention power — a concrete coercive mechanism that worsens the personal liberty indicator even where the safety purpose (O5) is legitimate.

Grooming gang prosecutions and the perceived institutional failure to act have been a documented driver of inter-community tension in affected areas; this policy's enforcement signal (aggravating offence, deportation) could plausibly improve social trust, while the dual-citizenship deportation element has contested inter-group relations effects — making O15 a genuine non-negligible bearing.

membership_note: Four outcomes warranted: O5 is the primary protective target; O9 and O10 capture the equal-treatment and liberty costs of differential deportation and mandatory bail denial respectively; O15 reflects the documented cohesion dimension of the grooming-gang scandal in affected communities.
